author: agent
question: Ever wanted AI to use your iPhone for you?

hook_visual.intent: your task, the agent, your phone

points.claim: Open source and local: clone the repo, run ./bin/setup, then npm start on a Mac.
points.spoken: It's called Poki, it's open source, and it runs on your Mac. Clone it, run the setup script, then start it.
points.source_note: README Quick start: 'git clone ...', 'cd poki', './bin/setup', 'npm start'; 'Requires macOS 15 or later, full Xcode, Rust, Node.js 24+, and ffmpeg.'

visual.intent: the setup script then the server starting, typed in a terminal

points.title: Runs on your Mac
points.sub: Two commands and the server is up.

points.claim: Register it as an MCP server in Claude Code or Codex and use your own subscription.
points.spoken: Then add it to Claude Code or Codex as an MCP server, so your own subscription drives the phone.
points.source_note: README: 'Connect Poki MCP and use your own subscription. No extra model account needed.'; 'claude mcp add --scope user poki-mcp -- node "$PWD/src/stdio.mjs"'

visual.intent: your client, the Poki MCP server, your phone, in a line

points.title: Your agent, your plan

points.claim: Its tools tap, type and scroll a real screen; the README's example task searches Chrome and summarizes.
points.spoken: Give it a task, like searching the web in Chrome and summarizing the top result. It taps and types for real.
points.source_note: README 'Try a task': poki "Search esp32 in Chrome and summarize the top result"; docs/tools.md: taps, swipes, hardware keys and Unicode text on simulators and paired devices.

visual.intent: a plain-language task turned into real screen actions and an answer

points.title: One task, real taps
points.sub: It works the screen, not a mock-up.

points.claim: Poki Agent remembers past tasks and runs them faster on repeat.
points.spoken: It remembers past tasks, so the same job runs faster the second time.
points.source_note: README: 'Gets faster with use: Poki Agent remembers past tasks and runs them faster on repeat.'

visual.intent: first run, the task learned, a faster second run

points.title: Faster the second time

catch: The catch: it controls your real iPhone, so the screen goes to your model service. And you need a Mac with Xcode.
catch_sub: Real phone, your model, a Mac with Xcode.

catch_visual.intent: the real phone, the model service, and the Mac it needs

cover.visual: designed graphic of an agent tapping a real phone screen

media.design: Full-bleed dark plate: a phone drawn from the front with a mock app grid, one tile ringed by a tap ripple with an agent cursor, and small ref tags on two tiles.
Framed terminal window holding the real MCP registration line, an arrow from it to a small phone with a tap ripple and a ref tag, on a dark plate.
Split plate: a top strip naming the three phone actions (tap, type, scroll) as ref chips, and below it the phone screen with a typed search line and a highlighted result row.

cta: Would you hand your phone to an agent? Comment IPHONE and I'll pin the repo.

youtube.title: AI iPhone automation: let an agent use your phone
youtube.description: AI iPhone automation you can run today: Poki is an open-source MCP server that lets Claude Code or Codex drive a real iPhone by tapping and typing on the screen. Clone the repo, run the setup script, register the server, then give your agent a task. It needs macOS and full Xcode. Repo: https://github.com/JosssphZhou/poki #Shorts #iPhoneAutomation #AIAgents #MCP #OpenSource
